overview: Breast cancer is a disease in which abnormal cells in the breast grow out of control and form tumours. If left unchecked, the tumours can spread throughout the body and become fatal. Breast cancer cells begin inside the milk ducts and/or the milk-producing lobules of the breast.
symptoms: a breast lump or thickening, often without pain
change in size, shape or appearance of the breast
dimpling, redness, pitting or other changes in the skin
abnormal or bloody fluid from the nipple
diagnosis: timely diagnosis and referral for treatment services
treatment: surgery to remove the breast tumour
medications to kill cancer cells and prevent spread
risk_factors: inherited high penetrance gene mutations (BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB-2)
complications: spread to nearby lymph nodes or other organs
key_facts: Breast cancer caused an estimated 670 000 deaths globally in 2022
Approximately 0.5–1% of breast cancers occur in men
